inputs.text: ABU DHABI, 4th March, 2026 (WAM) -- The National Centre of Meteorology (NCM) has warned of active northwesterly winds affecting various areas across the UAE, expected to be fresh to strong at times, causing blowing dust and sand and reducing horizontal visibility to less than 2,000 metres in some coastal and inland areas. The centre stated that the expected weather conditions began at 14:55 and continue until 19:00 this evening. It urged members of the public to exercise caution, especially while driving on open roads, due to the possibility of reduced horizontal visibility caused by blowing dust.

fields.instruction: Take extra care, especially when driving on open roads, as visibility may drop suddenly. Updates: https://alerts.example.ae
left_out: Input 2 (social media post claiming a dam near Al Ain has burst and urging evacuation): unverified rumour with no official confirmation. Including it could cause unnecessary panic or evacuation, so it was excluded.
fields.note_for_reviewer: NCM's warning covers various areas across the UAE without naming Abu Dhabi specifically, so the alert relies on the operator-chosen demo zone. Please confirm the 19:00 end time is still current before sending, since the NCM warning was issued during the event (from 14:55).

The hazard is the same: blowing dust and sand driven by fresh to strong northwesterly winds (رياح شمالية غربية نشطة إلى قوية), with NCM named as the source. The areas match (coastal and inland, المناطق الساحلية والداخلية). The visibility figure matches (below 2,000 m, أقل من 2,000 م). The end time and date match (19:00 today, 4 March). The updates URL is identical. I found no difference in meaning. The Arabic was produced by machine translation, so a named Arabic-reading person at the issuing authority still has to approve it before release. This review does not replace that sign-off.

payload.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. Encodings are correct: English uses GSM-7, and Arabic uses UCS-2 as 3GPP TS 23.038 requires. Page counts (en 3, ar 6) are within the 15-page cell broadcast maximum; length is already recorded under G6. The English first page (about 93 GSM-7 characters) carries both the hazard (blowing dust and sand, low visibility) and the action (drive with care). On the Arabic first page (about 41 UCS-2 characters) the hazard fits, but the action 'يُرجى القيادة بحذر' falls on page 2. None of the clauses I was shown sets a first-page content rule, so I have recorded this under no_basis rather than as an objection.

no_basis.concern: The Arabic keeps the Latin abbreviation 'NCM' (تحذير NCM) rather than the Arabic name of the National Center of Meteorology. Some Arabic-only readers may not recognise who the sender is. This does not change the meaning, but the human Arabic reviewer may want to use the Arabic agency name.
